RL2: "Hey, you made it. All right." / RL2: "Okay, here's how it works around here. The only currency worth shit is rough diamonds. Don't accept paper money from anybody. I wouldn't wipe my ass with it. You do work for the UFLL -- you get paid in stones." / RL2: "Now... One of my guys - not the sharpest blade in the set - picked up a case of diamonds and dropped 'em off here yesterday. He stuck 'em somewhere in the camp and promptly got shot in the head back in town. Maybe *you* killed him. Anyway, if you want those rocks go outside and find 'em. The case has a tracker you can home in on with your compass." / RL2: "Hey! He's coming out." / RL2: "Hasta luego." / RL2: "You don't hear too good, do you? I said you’re sick, don’t waste time." / RL2: "If I were you, I'd go buy some medicine first. That malaria is nothing to screw around with. You'll probably have some luck over at Mike's bar. All those expat cabrones drink there. Get yourself healthy and come by the Front's office in town. I'll introduce you to Gakumba. Get you hooked up." / RL2: "Whatever."

Remember to give the DJ my message... and THEN blow that antennae to hell." / Andre, BAH: "That sounded great! The militia are coming now! BAH: "It’s easy as hell for you. All you’ve got to do is go to the reservoir pumphouse and destroy the equipment inside." / BAH: "It’s where they control the waterflow. Automatic cutoff system and all that. - So when you blow the pipeline, the water will flood the whole canyon. AND the diamond mine." / BAH: "That mine is a joke There are no diamonds in there. Never have been." / BAH: "Get this. I’ve been working "security" there." / BAH: "Those idiots said they’re gonna fire me...please." / BAH: "Listen. I’ll be at the mine when it floods. Those guys’ll probably blame me and then try to kill my ass. So help a brother out. All right?" / BAH: "Come on man. Don’t be like that." / BAH: "All you’ve got to do is find the pumphouse and destroy the controls first!" / BAH: "Hey man. - I’ve got a proposition for you. A way you can really wreak some havoc with that pipeline." / BAH: "All right, man!" / BAH: "Hmmm." / Andre, BAH: "It’s Andre. I know what you've been up to... Come meet me up the hill from the levee." / Andre, BAH: "Good job. The cutoff system is shot. Now go get that pipeline." / Andre, BAH: "Ohh shit here comes the water. Place will be flooded out in no time. I love it!" / Andre, BAH: "They found me out! - I need your help!" / Andre, BAH: "Hello? You forgetting something? Like a perfectly good plan...?"

BAH: "I know those boys want you to blow up the truck." / BAH: "Naw, man. Don’t do that. Go over to the post office instead." / BAH: "Grab this package. It’s got a distributor cap in it." / BAH: "Fits your truck. You getting the picture?" / BAH: "Once the truck is running again, drive it over to my garage." / BAH: "Where I work." / BAH: "You drive it in, nice and slow…we leave…and then we ignite those tanks. Make everything burn." / BAH: "I’m leaving my ID papers in there, where they WON’T burn. So when my… old employers find em, they’ll assume I died in the fire and get off my ass." / BAH: "Now listen, man. You have got to be careful. You don’t want to start trouble too soon. Be cool when you drive into the garage. You cause trouble, then I’m leaving you behind. All right?" / BAH: "Come on, man. Don’t be like that." / BAH: "The package is in the post office!" / BAH: "Looking sharp, man." / BAH: "Over here!" / BAH: "Trouble?" / Andre, BAH: "Hey man. Your meeting over? It’s Andre. Do me a favor and meet me near the post office." / Andre, BAH: "Got the package? Then it’s time to find the truck, bro." / Andre, BAH: "I’m at the garage waiting for you, man." / BAH: "Shit, man. Where are you? I’ve been waiting." / Andre, BAH: "What did you do? My little plan is good and screwed. I'm gone."

BAH: "You go on and open up one of those tanks." / BAH: "OK bro. We got to move." / BAH: "Hey man this is no time to be messing around!" / BAH: "Good work. - Now I’m gonna short out this junction box. All right?"

BAH: "What’s up!" / BAH: "All you do is go to the outpost up the road." / BAH: "Find the man inside, and kill him, before you do anything else..." / BAH: "Easy." / BAH: "He’s the teamster, see. He delivers medicine to the medics. With him dead, I can read his orders. Finally find out where they store all the good shit." / BAH: "They've managed to keep their secret til now. They're supposed to have a good hiding spot worked out." / BAH: "With your mission, I think we have the perfect time to hit both their production... and their inventory." / BAH: "You proceed to your main target. The kilns. While they're busy dealing with you, I'll use the information I take off the dead driver." / BAH: "Your call." / BAH: "He’s at the outpost!" / BAH: "I like this job they gave you. Let’s make it better." / BAH: "Blow up their stores of artemisia. Wherever it happens to be." / BAH: "Standing by then." / Andre, BAH: "It’s Andre Hyppolite. I want to talk with you about this new job. Meet me on the Dogon River delta. All right?" / Andre, BAH: "We’re in business. Take care of those kilns. I'll go through the driver's things." / Andre, BAH: "Hey, it's me. I found their cache. A buried storehouse in some Dogon ruins to the north. Meet me there when you're finished." / Andre, BAH: "Hey... it's me again... I'm the thick of it. I could use your assistance." / Andre, BAH: "Hey... Good job on the kilns, but I'm afraid you scared away our man. I'll have to find another way to find those stores... Too bad."

BAH: "You need to kill Yabek, Well I can help you do it. And with a little style." / BAH: "I’ve got this bomb. Wait’ll you see it. Over a thousand pounds, good to go. All it needs is the fuse." / BAH: "Which you can bring me. There's a salvage site west of here." / BAH: "Then we can blow up the bridge where Yabek’s hiding." / BAH: "Nothing but a grease puddle left when we’re done." / BAH: "He’s got to go. - Guy talks way too much. He’s been telling people I’ve got ties with the CIA. The Medellin cartel. I mean shit! Where does he get these stupid ideas?" / BAH: "I gotta warn you. This bridge, it’s big. The APR troops will come after us for sure. We’ll have to fight our way out of there…" / BAH: "It’s your world…" / BAH: "The fuse is at this salvage site, out in the desert! - You can’t miss it!" / BAH: "Nice to see you." / BAH: "Hey." / BAH: "Yeah. I get you." / Andre, BAH: "Good. I caught you. It’s Andre. Meet me up near Sepoko, all right?" / Andre, BAH: "Got the fuse? Meet me at the bridge." / Andre, BAH: "Hello...? You know I'm not exactly inconspicuous with this giant bomb mounted on my truck... Bad time for you to start improvising, my friend. See ya."

BAH: "OK. Now give me the fuse. - But please. No sudden moves." / BAH: "All right. Here goes." / BAH: "Do me a favor, man. Keep an eye out." / BAH: "That’s it!" / BAH: "Let’s take cover." / BAH: "Over there." / BAH: "Heads down -" / BAH: "You want to see this bad boy blow up, you better give me that fuse." / BAH: "Today, my man!" / BAH: "Holy mother of GOD. That was awesome." / BAH: "They’re on their way for sure now." / BAH: "Check it out man." / BAH: "We're safe!" / BAH: "Hey! - What you doing? - It’s me!"

BAH: "I’ve got the inside dope on that polytech teacher for you." / BAH: "But first I need you to do me a favor. Go to the border crossing and find the telecom station. Inside you’ll find a binder. Take it for me?" / BAH: "Inside the binder are all the maps, marking the locations of the cellphone towers." / BAH: "Pilots use them as landmarks." / BAH: "Before you kill the instructor, make him use his Sat-phone and call his pilot." / BAH: "Give him the new coordinates. Then the pilot will deliver the package to us instead. See?" / BAH: "It’s smart. We used to run the same operation with the cartels back in Haiti. Except back then it was coca, not band-aids." / BAH: "I’ll grab the package, we’ll sell the stuff, and split the profits 50/50. Easy day’s work." / BAH: "What’s up?" / BAH: "Look for the binder!" / BAH: "Salut." / BAH: "Careful my friend!" / BAH: "Uh-huh." / Andre, BAH: "You sure do spend a lot of time with those warlords, man. It’s Andre. Come over and meet me at rubbish dump north of the airport when you get a chance." / Andre, BAH: "You’re all clear for the Polytechnique. Good luck." / Andre, BAH: "It worked! I can see the plane now. I’ll call you back as soon as I have the package." / Andre, BAH: "Merde! The wind blew the package right onto the strip! I’m surrounded by the APR! Get your ass over here, bro!" / Andre, BAH: "Are you an amateur? Forget about it. Some other time maybe."

BAH: "You know what we are carrying. - The Lieutenant and his crazy ideas, eh?" / BAH: "When our cargo reaches Port Selao, things are going to get very bad, very quickly." / BAH: "Can I suggest you go and find Doctor Obua at the clinic? Warn him that he is going to have a busy night. - Thankless work, being a doctor in this country." / BAH: "I plan to leave once delivery is complete. I’ll go over to the other side of Lake Segolo. Lay low." / BAH: "You will too, if you know what’s good for you." / BAH: "But first, we have to make this delivery! - You go out on deck. Keep a watch out for anybody who takes an interest in our small vessel." / BAH: "I’m Andre Hyppolite. I’ll be your captain tonight." / BAH: "Go to the hatch!"
BAH: "Take the back door. - Less men out there." / BAH: "My name is Andre. - You ever need any help, I’ll do what I can." / BAH: "Welcome to Port Selao!" / BAH: "Wait! Not that way."

BAH: "Jesus! - Get in here, now!" / BAH: "I thought I was dead for sure. Front troops on one side, APR troops on the other…shooting at each other, shooting at me…mon dieu, what a nightmare." / BAH: "This barge is useless now. I might as well sink it and take a look around…fate must have brought me here for a reason, right?" / BAH: "Wait. I haven’t finished." / BAH: "Come back sometime. I’ll be here." / BAH: "Hurry. Get inside." / BAH: "I’m in here!" / Andre, BAH: "The Lieutenant’s plan worked. The guns are in Port Selao. But now I’ve got gunboats on my ass. I’ve gotta get rid of this barge, quick! Come help me if you can - I’m headed to the far side of the lake!" / Andre, BAH: "I’m caught in a crossfire! The barge is dead in the water... Please get over here!" / BAH: "But look, man... We're still in the shit. I can't do anything about anything until those troops are neutralized. Can you deal with it?"

BAH: "Got a second?" / BAH: "Don’t believe what they’re telling you about the ceasefire. It’s a death sentence for guys like you and me." / BAH: "Listen. Do what they’re asking you to do. Pick up the diamonds. But  once you’ve got them, bring them to the airfield." / BAH: "We’ll be there waiting. We’ve arranged for a pilot to exfil us out of here, but he won’t do shit unless we pay him. - Which we will. - With the diamonds." / BAH: "Wait." / BAH: "This is important." / BAH: "Bring the diamonds." / BAH: "Come here. I have to talk to you."

BAH: "Hey. - Hey. - Over here." / BAH: "I tried to warn you, didn’t I? About those warlords? - And where the fuck were you with the diamonds?" / BAH: "The pilot left us behind, man. I told you he would if we couldn’t pay him. - Then the soldiers showed up. Took us all in. I don’t know if any of the other guys made it." / BAH: "The factions are blaming the assassination on us. They’re saying all the foreigners are to blame, and that they have to get rid of us. For the good of the country." / MPG1 (DIALD) / BAH: "Good... You look like garbage." / BAH (DIALE)

BAH: "Oh thank God it’s you." / BAH: "I…I don’t think I can go anywhere yet." / BAH: "Go ahead. - I’ll catch up." / BAH: "I’ll be all right." / BAH: "Can’t get any worse than this, right?" / BAH: "... who ... sacre coeur ..." / BAH (WAITA) / BAH: "... yeah ... go ..." / BAH (DIALD)

BAH: "Everything’s cool now. It’s cool." / BAH: "You’re wasting time. Shoot him." / BAH: "Hey! - Relax! Nobody needs to do anything stupid here." / BAH: "Don’t bother trying to leave. You won’t get far." / BAH: "Fuck you -" / BAH: "And now you’re here. What a coincidence." / BAH: "Look! I’ve got the diamonds." / BAH: "I’m sorry." / BAH: "Shut up. We made our deal. He’s on his own."

BAH: "Hey!" / BAH: "There may be more guards out there." / BAH: "Where are the guards?" / BAH: "You killed them, didn’t you." / BAH: "I don’t know why you did that, but it's good news for me. My name's Andre." / BAH: "Let’s get out of here, hein?" / BAH: "But not together. We have better chance if we are apart." / BAH: "I think for this, I owe you at least one drink, later sometime. N’est-ce pas?" / BAH: "I’m in here! - Hey!"

BAH: "Please help... A snake bit me… Poisonous... Anti-venom... Please... Need a shot... Please..." / BAH (DIALA) / BAH: "Au voir, man. Thank you." / BAH: "My name is Andre. Andre Hyppolite. I guess I owe you." / BAH: "H-hey... Help me... help..." / BAH: "Okay. Not bad. Just gonna wait here a bit." / BAH: "Okay... I made it... <weak laugh> I can't believe it." / BAH (WAITA)
BAH: "Okay yeah -- I heard what you did for Marty… But I’d help you anyway. You seem like an all right guy."
BAH: "My friend. I was very sorry to hear about Marty Alencar. But at least you were there."
BAH: "You know – I was thinking about what happened to Marty… I hope it was quick for him. I really do."
BAH: "Anyway, it’s the very least I can do. You came through for me on that last job. Not everyone would have."
BAH: "And by the way… I heard what you did for Frank out there. You’re a good man."
BAH: "And… I heard about Bilders. I know he was a friend of yours. Sorry man."
BAH: "Listen. The business with Frank Bilders... Truly a shame. I don’t know what else to say."
BAH: "And hey – I know how you stood with Echebbi during that latest misadventure of his. I admire that."
BAH: "Before you go… I wanted to say I’m sorry about Hakim. I didn’t know him very well. He was a professional."
BAH: "Listen. What happened to Mr. Echebbi, that… Well it’s a terrible thing."
BAH: "Hey. The Davar woman told me about how you ran in and saved the day... I never knew you were so gallant."
BAH: "About Nasreen. You did everything you could, I hope you know that. Her story was never going to have a happy ending."
BAH: "How well did you know Nasreen? I know she was brave. However it happened, I know she went out fighting."
BAH: "And another thing! I want to thank you for watching out for Xianyong during that latest thing… He’s just a kid. Invincible. Lucky."
BAH: "Before you go… Xianyong was my friend too. I’m glad you were by his side at the end. In our profession, sometimes that’s all you can hope for."
BAH: "Listen. I knew Xianyong. The Chinese kid. Not well, but I was sad to hear how it went down for him. He deserved better than this place."

BFG: "Over here!" / BFG: "Hey, it’s me! You know?" / BFG: "You want some company? I can stick around for a while." / BFG: "You got that look in your eye. You’re up to no good. - You want some help with whatever you got planned?" / BFG: "It’s bad out here today. You want me to stick around, in case you run into any trouble?" / BFG: "No problem." / BFG: "Bueno. - OK. - We’re together." / BFG: "I’ll be here." / BFG: "OK…" / BFG: "Lone Ranger rides alone." / BFG: "See you later…" / BFG: "Be safe." / BFG: "Watch yourself." / BFG: "Good luck." / BFG: "How are you doing." / BFG: "Long time no see." / BFG: "What's up?"

BFG: "Over here." / BFG: "I just learned of a large weapons supply. A man I know, he told me he has been hiding them at his ranch house." / BFG: "The APR has seized his home, you see. He is afraid they will find his guns and then things will get very bad around here." / BFG: "The weapons are hidden in his house. I am looking for someone willing to go there and destroy the cache. - Maybe you?" / BFG: "Bueno. We already have enough weapons around here!" / BFG: "Wait, there’s more!" / BFG (EXITB) / BFG: "Let me know how it goes." / BFG: "It’s good that you’re here."
BFG: "Hello." / BFG: "How did it go? Did you find the ranch house okay?" / BFG: "So. No more guns for APR." / BFG: "Any news?" / BFG: "Too bad." / BFG: "Hola."

BFG (BECKN) / BFG: "There is a convoy of trucks passing through today." / BFG: "Carrying new furniture for Mbantuwe’s mansion. - Can you believe that? His people starve in the street, and he buys gold-plated dishes. It’s obscene." / BFG: "I would destroy the convoy myself if I could. But I have to meet a contact here in an hour. Will you do the job for me?" / BFG: "Mbantuwe will just have to make do." / BFG: "Don’t you want to know what they’re carrying?" / BFG: "God dammit." / BFG: "Good luck." / BFG: "I have a favor to ask you."
BFG: "Look who’s here." / BFG: "How is the convoy?" / BFG: "Mbantuwe will be very angry." / BFG: "What happened?" / BFG: "Too bad for him, eh?" / BFG: "Hola."

BFG: "Hey it’s you!" / BFG: "You still have that malaria, though, don’t you." / BFG: "You see that man over there?" / BFG: "He has medicine. You ask him, he might give some to you." / BFG: "You ever get in a bad spot while you’re here, you find me. OK? This place is rough. Everybody needs a friend." / BFG: "You’ll see soon how bad it is. - The war here is out of control. It’s not even a real war anymore. Just a, mm how you say, a free-for-all." / BFG: "If the two factions disappeared, the people here might have a chance." / BFG: "But they’re not going anywhere until somebody makes them." / BFG: "I’d do it myself if I could." / BFG: "I know you remember me!" / BFG: "Take those pills, compay…you need them." / BFG: "I see you around." / BFG: "How are you. - You made it out. - I didn’t introduce myself before. My name is Flora Guillen."

BFG: "I think I know who you are. People are talking about you." / BFG: "Muy bien. - You ever need any help, come find me. - My name is Guillen." / BFG: "And stay away from the factions. They’re animals. Both sides." / BFG: "Adios." / BFG (EXITB) / BFG: "Si…Bueno…"

BFG: "There’s a fishing village downriver." / BFG: "He won’t be a moving target anymore. Much easier to kill." / BFG: "Good luck with that ambush." / BFG: "Won’t work unless you get that ledger. It’s in that fishing village. Look for the brother’s house!" / BFG: "The police-man's brother lives there. You should pay him a visit." / BFG: "He’s hiding a ledger. It lists all the bribes the constable's taken from APR over the years." / BFG: "When jefe finds out you’ve got the book, he’ll run back to his police station like a little boy and try to hide." / BFG: "I hear the deputy hates his boss. When he finds out about the APR bribes, I figure he’ll hand over all the police weapons over to the UFLL, just to make a point." / BFG: "That’s when I’m going to ambush their convoy and wreck those weapons." / BFG: "If you help me out, you can have anything that's left." / BFG (EXITA) / BFG: "Don’t bother chasing after the federale’s motorcade. There’s a better way to get the job done." / Flora, BFG: "Come meet me north of the cattle market. I have news that can help you." / Flora, BFG: "The chief got the message about the ledger. He’s heading back to his post right now." / Flora, BFG: "I was right about the deputy. The convoy’s moving out right now. Come meet me and we’ll take care of them together." / Flora, BFG: "I’ve got them. But I can’t do this alone. Come over here!" / Flora, BFG: "Did you kill him? That was short-sighted of you. But your call, I guess."

BFG: "Mister, you can be a real pain when you like... I had this all wrapped up. Big waste of time. Adios." / BFG: "Time for work." / BFG: "There’s a cattle ranch," / BFG: "I need you to execute him." / BFG: "I need those men to deploy. Now." / BFG: "Total hardass." / BFG (EXITA) / BFG: "Your momma didn’t teach you very good manners." / BFG: "half a kilometer east of here." / BFG: "There's a Front official who lives there." / BFG: "There’s an entire UFLL platoon sitting on a troop train, right now. But this fraud at the ranch has ordered them to stand down. He has some side deal going. He intends to rent them out." / BFG: "The commander of those troops is a high-value target. Ex Gurkha Regiment." / BFG: "I’m going to take that man off the table today." / BFG: "That train's going to derail. And when it does, I'll close in to verify the Ghurka is dead." / BFG: "That means I’ll be in the middle of the wreck site when any survivors manage to regroup." / BFG: "I won’t be able to get out of there on my own. I’ll be surrounded. I need you to rendezvous and give me cover." / BFG: "This won’t work unless you kill the crook at the ranch." / BFG: "You’re doing something with the APR. Well I can help you. If you help me." / Flora, BFG: "I need to speak to you. Meet me east of the railyard." / Flora, BFG: "Nice work with that idiot... Guess you better go start some trouble at the railyard!" / Flora, BFG: "Okay, the train's rolling... I'm gonna go stop it the hard way. Meet me up the tracks as soon as you can." / Flora, BFG: "I swept the train... I've confirmed the kill... Where are you...?!"

BFG: "I need it." / BFG: "Think you can get it for me?" / BFG: "Because they’re all carrying gas, and everybody wants gas around here." / BFG: "Except maybe me." / BFG: "It might get hairy. I could use your help getting out of there." / BFG: "I thought I could trust you." / BFG: "Look for the map in the manager’s office!" / BFG: "So they’re paying you to take out the motor pool." / BFG: "So is the UFLL, frankly." / BFG: "Hey. Over here." / BFG: "You know the big oil terminal, north of here?" / BFG: "The Front has an office there. Inside the office, there’s a map." / BFG: "The map shows the routes that their trucks follow. They change the routes every other day, so nobody can track them." / BFG: "After you blow up the motorpool, every one of those drivers is going to return to the terminal as fast as they can." / BFG: "The trucks are disguised. The UFLL keeps their fuel reserve on wheels so they can keep it mobile... nobody can attack it." / BFG: "I’m going to ambush the trucks as they come in. I’ll try to steal one and blow up the rest. Or maybe blow them all up. I haven’t decided yet." / BFG: "APR's destroying this entire country." / Flora, BFG: "It’s Flora. Meet me just over the hill from the cattle ranch." / Flora, BFG: "I’ll start setting up. Hit the motor pool whenever you’re ready." / Flora, BFG: "All the trucks are heading this way. I’m on the edge of the landfill if you want to watch this. It’s going to be good." / Flora, BFG: "I’ve got one tanker down! Exchanging fire with driver and soldiers! Get over here if you can!" / Flora, BFG: "(grumbles) -- Couldn't do this one little thing?"

Flora, BFG: "Maldito -- ! What is your damage? Forget what's at stake...? Mi culo! I gotta get out of here..." / BFG: "Sorry. None of my business. It’s just -" / BFG (BECKN) / BFG: "There’s an informant at the villa. He’s in contact with those Special Forces men you're after. If you can get to this guy, you can force him to send the wrong instructions." / BFG: "This will lead them to Mokuba - the shantytown. And that’s where the APR is going to ambush them." / BFG: "The informant’s Belgian." / BFG: "An unusual guy. Hard to miss." / BFG: "Hate to lay traps, but I have no choice. They’re here to get me." / BFG: "Look. I stole medical supplies. OK? And I sold them on the black market." / BFG: "What else was I supposed to do? The factions keep all the medicine for themselves. I tried to strike a deal with the APR." / BFG: "I’ll have to go to the shantytown. If you can meet me there later and help me deal with these guys, I’d appreciate it." / BFG (EXITA) / BFG: "You're in a hurry, I see." / BFG: "The Belgian will tell you he’s working for foreign press! Don’t believe it!" / BFG: "You need to seriously ask yourself why you’re playing these games with the factions..." / Flora, BFG: "Find me half a klick south of the OGC Greenhouses. It’s important." / Flora, BFG: "It must have worked, the Special Forces men are heading towards Mokuba now." / Flora, BFG: "I'm with the men from the APR... You didn't just burn that truck, did you...? Christ... Okay, this is bad. You better come find me!" / Flora, BFG: "Dammit! These guys are blaming me for the loss of those supplies... Get over here! Please!"

BFG: "The UFLL is doing the right thing, for once. - For the wrong reasons, of course." / BFG: "You know where the chemical dump is? Over by the railspur?" / BFG: "There’s a small tank over there." / BFG: "Think you could get it for me?" / BFG: "And then when everything dies, maybe then people will notice." / BFG: "For months, I’ve been flying for this company, dropping their pesticide. I TELL people how bad they are. They won’t listen. - Maybe now they will." / BFG: "I’ll call you from the air. Make sure you’re all right." / BFG: "God dammit. I was talking to you." / BFG: "I need the tank at the chemical dump! Be sure not to get any on your skin!" / BFG: "OK. Let’s talk. BMA: "Just gonna come out and say this – I’m not gonna second-guess you, just because of what happened to Hakim. He was a professional, and he knew the risks."
BMA: "Maybe it’s not my place to say, but I’m glad to see you’re still at it. Losing Echebbi was a bad hit. But you’ve got to send a message to these viado shit-bags."
BMA: "You’re a lucky sonofabitch. I got the full ‘after-action’ on that last gig of yours. Sounds like Nasreen Davar almost got both your asses shot up."
BMA: "Crazy thing about Nasreen. I don’t just mean her dying. You ever do any background on her? No wonder she never talked politics. Regardless, she was a warrior."
BMA: "Yeah, well… (clucks) Our luck’s got to change at some point. After Nasreen, you know… We’re due, man."
BMA: "Hey, good job on the Xianyong Bai exfil… You saved that guy’s bacon proper. That earns you serious points around here."
BMA: "Oh. Hey. Full props to you, going in after Xianyong Bai like you did. Might not be much consolation, but you did as much as anyone could have. Sorry man."
BMA: "Here’s the thing. Dude like Xianyong goes pretty far on balls and luck. That’s how it goes. You don’t smarten up quick, and the luck gets used up. Poor bastard."

BMD: "Haven’t seen a new face here for a long time." / BMD: "If you ever need help, come find me." / BMD: "I’ve been here for a while. I know how things work." / BMD: "Even in hell, things get done." / BMD (EXITA) / BMD: "I’ll see you later!" / BMD: "Salut. I am Michele."

BMD: "It will involve lots of explosions." / BMD: "But that happens later." / BMD: "On the wall. BMD: "Bon." / BMD: "Good. Good." / BMD: "The repairs are almost complete. No problem getting the tank, I hope?"

The APR patrols won't stay away for much longer." / Michele, BMD: "You just decided to do things your own way? You know, there are other things at stake, than just... Anyway. I'm going."

BMD: "Over here!" / BMD: "It's INSANE... They were on us like rabid dogs... How long have they been planning this!?" / BMD: "They’re coming, you know. - I mean ALL of them." / BMD: "Thank you for staying... It's the only way we'll survive this..." / BMD: "No please come back!!" / BMD: "How can you do this to us." / BMD: "Quickly. Get inside." / BMD: "Stay back. -- All of you." / BMD: "Help me move this refrigerator. We’ve got to block the door."
BMD: "Goodbye -" / BMD: "Shut up. We made our deal. He’s on his own." / BMD: "Quit wasting time. Just shoot him."

BMD: "Please. Let me out." / BMD: "Go to Mike’s. It is a bar. I will meet you there and help you get the medicine you need. - OK?" / BMD: "Hey... My name's Michele. Thank you." / BMD: "Who are you? Why are you here?" / BMD: "You are sick! - You have malaria." / BMD: "Thank God." / BMD: "This prison is a hellhole. I have to get out." / BMD: "I don’t know why you’re here…" / BMD: "And I don’t care." / BMD: "We have to leave separately. - We’ll move faster that way. - More guards are coming. - They always do." / BMD: "Hey! - Hey! - Qui est là?" / BMD: "We must leave separately. - We’ll move faster that way."

BMD: "Here….I’m over here…" / BMD: "Please…I have to get off this mountain." / BMD: "In my bag. I have medicine. - I need you to give me a shot." / BMD: "Thank you... You have no idea..." / BMD: "I can make it... I’ll go down the hill... There’s a clinic nearby... It's better if you leave... If the wrong people find us together, things will go badly..." / BMD: "One more thing... I'm Michele... I promise I'll keep my eye out for you... Thanks." / BMD: "Oh thank God." / BMD: "There was a crash. The plane just fell apart." / BMD: "I’ve been up here three days. - I think my rib is broken."
BMD: "And why shouldn’t I agree to work with you? You have an impressive record so far, no? Even Flora had to admit, you came through when it really mattered."
BMD: "You know, I haven’t been able to stop thinking about Flora. I’ve seen many people die here. Many women. But she kept her chin up, somehow. I’m glad she was not alone when she finally fell."

BMD: "Sorry… This latest thing – what happened to Flora. I didn’t know her very well. We didn’t have much in common. I wish I could have been a better friend to her. I don’t think she had many friends."
BMD: "And by the way, I was very relieved to hear that you and Josip made it through your misadventure intact. You were lucky, and so was he – to have an ally like you."
BMD: "But listen. It’s stupid of me to act like everything’s fine. Josip was my friend, too. I can only imagine what the two of you went through in that battle. I’m so sorry."

BMD: "Yes, of course. I heard about Mr. Idromeno. It is an awful thing. He was very kind to me. He understood about my mission here. It makes me sad to think his own children will never see him again."
BMD: "You know, you’ve been acting like a complete cowboy… That latest stunt with Marty Alencar. You’re both lucky you made it out in one piece. He won’t say it, but he’s grateful to you."
BMD: "I’m sorry about your friend… Marty was a true comrade. A soldier through and through. He loved this life, no matter the danger. I think he imagined his death would be much like this."
BMD: "But look – What happened to Marty… There aren’t words to describe the tragedy of that. It’s senseless. But it seems to happen here."
BMD: "And besides, cher -- I am still breathing thanks to you! You held up your end of the bargain last time. The least I can do is return the favor…"

BMD: "So Ferenc made it! It’s so ridiculous. He dragged you into one of his half-baked schemes, and then almost got his head blown off for his troubles. Good thing for him you’re one of the reliable ones."

BMD: "I haven’t said anything about Ferenc… I hope you know how sorry I am. He always acted like he was too good for this life, but deep down I think he knew he was born to it. I’m glad you were there during that fight."
BMD: "I was sorry to hear about Paul… I liked him. In spite of everything that’s happened here, I really expected him to be one of the survivors. It’s such a shame."
BMD: "It sounds like you and Quarbani Singh had a near-miss! You need to be careful, cher. Men like him are strong leaders, but they sometimes motivate the people around them a little too well…"
BMD: "Quarbani’s death… I want you to know how sorry I am. He was a colleague. Probably the most professional man I’ve ever met. You know he respected you..."
BMD: "Singh is gone. It’s just terrible. He seemed so impervious. I couldn’t imagine the force required to knock the man down, let alone end his life. I hope his family will be okay."

BMD: "By the way, don’t get any strange ideas about me… I’m no Warren Clyde. I heard about his insane scheme, and how you had to come bail him out of certain death…! Let’s stick to more conventional ops for now, hm?"
BMD: "I can’t tell you how sorry I am -- about Warren. For all his eccentric behavior, he was an asset. A loyal ally. I guess there’s some consolation in knowing that he went out fighting."

BMD: "I can’t believe Warren is just… gone. That ridiculous man. It’s a terrible loss, you know. He wasn’t just some American buffoon. He would happily have taken a bullet for any of us. I guess in the end he did."

BND: "Hello!" / BND: "Good for you. BND: "Of course, it doesn’t hurt that you and Marty Alencar managed to walk out of that last situation relatively unscathed. I feel you’re a dependable asset."

BND: "Not that I want you to get overconfident, but… It didn’t escape my attention that you managed to keep me alive on our last project."
BND: "There are some extravagant stories circulating – involving you and Hyppolite against a company of militia. You’re both breathing, so they must be true."

BND: "Your latest assignments sound like they ended well. Bilders is quite effective -- for such an eccentric. I’ve heard some intriguing stories about that man."
BND: "I was saddened to hear about Frank. Sometimes it feels like we bury our friends faster than we can make them here."
BND: "I don’t know if you’d heard, but Bilders was reported dead. You knew… It sounds like an ugly situation."
BND: "I heard it was you that extracted Echebbi after his last op. Hard to imagine someone as pragmatic as him blowing his cover, but regardless – You saved the day."

BND: "You were friends with Hakim Echebbi? I’m sorry for your loss. I guess former Naval commandos don’t often get to choose the circumstances of their deaths. It’s better for him that you were there."
BND: "How well did you know Hakim Echebbi? He was a player, underneath that family-man façade. Quite ruthless, actually. I’m sorry we lost him."
BND: "And as long as we’re on the subject – I hope you’re not being too reckless with Xianyong. He’s smart and has a lot of talent. But he needs to survive if it’s going to be developed…"
BND: "Sad news about Xianyong Bai. I didn’t get a chance to work with him, but what I heard was – well, anyway. I’m sorry you had to bear the burden of that."
BND: "By the way, I’ve learned a lot about our late friend, Xianyong. He had a remarkably rich career for someone so young. All of it illicit. Wasted potential now."

<tsk> Guy could have made way more money if he wanted to.

<whistle> This guy’s not kidding around with the merchandise! Look at this gun. -  “The Jackal.” What kind of name is that. - Guy is crazy! He practically give these things away! Why did he sell them so cheap?
They were cheap for the UFLL, too.
You good with a gun? You think you can hit a guy in a fast car?
It’s a big target. It’ll be easy to hit…
Is Kouassi talking to you, Quiepo? - No. He is talking to new guy.
Boss called. Said, “kill constable.” Hey! “No problem,” I said. “I know a guy.” You. Cause you’re hard.
He would be good. People know him.
You want a job? We got one. It’s good!
This man. This constable. He says he is going to give his men to UFLL.
Why? Why do this? APR is the greatest! - So you shoot him. OK? Then everybody knows how great APR is!
Quiepo. Tell him where to find this man.
He’s riding in a motorcade. It’s a moving target. You’ll have to pick a spot on the road and wait for him to come to you.
That little peanut will be in a great - big - SUV.
Tambossa told us where you can find this guy.
He’s in a motorcade. Couple of escort cars, lots of weapons. Best bet is to pick a spot and ambush him when he comes by.
Very easy. Not too many motorcades in this country of mine!
Ambush the motorcade and kill the cop. - And make it messy. We need you to send a message.
If you want, you kill all the guards too. Hey. No problem. - But be sure you get the constable. And do it so people see. OK? Everybody needs to know what happened!
I’ve got a good feeling about this. How bout we pay you right now for the work. Hm?
Ambush the motorcade, kill the police chief, and the job is complete.
People say a lot of crazy things.
I heard he’s got cancer, and only three months to live.
I also heard that somebody was paid to come here and kill him.
Who. The Jackal? - Come on. Guy’s an arms dealer. Who would want to kill a guy like that.
Well don’t just stand there. Come on in.
Sure. Maybe. - You want to make some money, son?
I’ve heard things about you. Terrible, evil things.
What the hell have you been doing, boy? They’ve been talking about you in every bodega from here to Katmandu! We’ve got some business to discuss.

So here’s the situation. - The UFLL has got a motor pool, over by the landfill. They use the place to fix their vehicles. - It’s all duct tape and baling wire over there, but somehow they manage to make it work.
We’re planning an attack on the UFLL motor pool. There are a hell of a lot of their vehicles on the road.
You know where the landfill is, right? Just west of here.
The motor pool’s over by the landfill, west of town. You can’t miss it. You sure as hell can’t miss the smell.
We need you to raise some hell. Take out their gear, set some stuff on fire…you get the idea. Just be sure you take out their air compressors. You copy? That’s the mission.

We - meaning Prosper and I - want you to find that motor pool and take it out. - This is fielder’s choice, all right? You handle it any way you like. It’s none of my damn business. Just be sure you take out their air compressors.
Today, you are being paid to blow things up! Tell me you do not love your job.
Here’s your money. Now get on out to that landfill and destroy those compressors.
Hey wow somebody is too important for us!
Yeah ok. Chop chop. I get it.
I consider it a serious problem. It would be easy for people to assume that I ordered this attack.
Look at their gear. Look what they’ve got. Jesus. That is highest quality.

If the people think I brought in this Special Forces team, then they will say: Gakumba is rich, taking their money and hiding it in secret bank accounts! Gakumba is buying entire armies, as easy as food off a shelf!
I wish you were rich. Then we would have some whoo-boy great stuff.
Damn. Look at that gun. I wonder if the Jackal can get us that.
How you get across border. Nobody can come into country these days.
You’re still around. Good. We need freelancer.
I need a man who can take a job and keep his mouth shut about it.
Nah. This guy doesn’t talk. He’s a pro.
You are a big man. Important. People talk to you. What are they saying about me?
Nobody knows nothing. Let’s talk business.
There is a Special Forces outfit in area. Just gun-for-hire guys. But they are armed to the teeth. They are paid to parachute in and grab someone -
He doesn’t need to know who.
There is a Special Forces team. Mercenaries. Extremely well equipped, these men.
They are here for a bigshot from the APR. But if they take our enemy, we got nobody to fight!
The SF team has set up in good position. In the desert. Two kilometers to southeast.
This team is waiting in the desert. Perhaps two kilometers southeast of here.
Here’s the problem. They’re here to take somebody from APR. And if they do it, people will think Gakumba planned it.
Gakumba here doesn’t want anybody to think HE plan secret rendition. Would make him look bad.
Enough please. All you have to do is find these men and destroy their vehicles.
The GEAR in their vehicle. Radios, water canteens, ammo, all that gear they dropped in.
Then people will think I am working with outsiders. This is no good!
So you must find their hiding-place and destroy their supplies.
Tough guys not so tough if they don’t have any bullets or MREs or water.
This is OUR struggle. Africa is for Africans. We do not need outside involvement! - I expect you to stop these men. Job is yours.
Standby point is in southern desert. Find the team and destroy their gear. Then they are nice and screwed. Payment's here.
So we’ll get to the point.
How did you let this happen?
Thank you for thinking that I control everything in this country.
Marron! This is obscene! They going to take that gold and won’t be nothing left! - WE were the ones. That old king came to us.
He talked to everybody. APR and UFLL. He has always played both ends against the middle. That is why he has the gold and we have this war.
This is wrong. APR’s gonna take all the gold. Then where we gonna be? Damn.
You want a job? We need a no-name scumbag like you.
You got some good timing, man.
You’re that guy. I been hearing about you.
Hey! Where have you been? We need to get you in with us.
You know this FUBAR country used to have a king? - I’m serious, man.
The hombre got a boatload of money from Europe, back in the day. And then he took off. But he’s back and he brought his gold with him.
Carbonell is very enthusiastic because our former king has returned.
And he brought his money with him.
Yes. Kgosi wants to return to his throne. He thinks it can be bought.
That gold comes from our mines. It belongs to us.
The gold is sitting out in an oasis in the northeastern desert. Millions of dollars! Sitting under a tarp!
All of it protected" by those stupid APR boys."
Hell YES it can be bought! - I'll sell it to him.
The gold is out at the northeastern oasis. The APR is guarding it.
Kgosi has brought his treasure to broker a peace agreement. What he doesn’t realize is that this is not possible.
We need some noname cabron like you to go out there and find the gold. Send a text message with the location.
Don't touch the treasure. It’s not yours.
Too much for one guy to carry, anyway.
We are not hiring you to take the gold. Only to kill the men guarding it.
Of course, we cannot send our men on this job. It must be an outside party. Like yourself.
Just need you to find it and text us the location on your mobile phone. That’s it.
The king thinks he can restore his legacy before he dies. Pass his throne on to his son. It will never happen. Not in my lifetime.
Got it? Hit the oasis. Kill the guards. Use your mobile to send us the location. It’s gonna be good.
Do not let us hold you up, sir.
You just completed your last mission for the APR.
This conflict with the APR. It has been going on for a long time. - Both sides tolerate the conflict, because we understand it.

But things have changed. You have changed them. The UFLL is almost unstoppable here - Even the party leader doesn't realize. So. I’ve decided to eliminate Kouassi and assert our control in the north. I will be the voice of stability. And peace.
You are the only person for this job.
It will only take one bullet.
Together, you and I can steer the future of this country.
Oh ho! Look who is here. The guy who works with everybody. - Well that’s about to end.
This is a good day for us, my friend!
You know, this thing with the UFLL, it has been going on a long time. - Both sides are used to it! Everybody understands it!
But I am a man of vision. The big man - Major Tambossa - said so himself.
The APR is stronger now than ever before! - Thanks to YOU, my friend! - So how about we make a REAL change. Destroy the UFLL in the north, once and for all!
You are the perfect one for the job.
He’s at his cabin up on Thabamolaetsa. He thinks it is hidden. But I know the way. You just follow the river and take the trail up to Goka Falls.
You come back when you are done and we will have a drink to celebrate! Here.
And more to come. This is a very rich country. And soon it will be - our country!
Now question is, what do I do with you.
Things have taken a turn for the worse. Leboa-Seko’s a mess. We need to deal with it. And my men are no use in their condition.
You want out of here? No problem. We’ll bring a truck around, leave it for you here at the shelter. But I require something.
You seem all right. No stab wounds. Head still attached to your body.
Listen up! We’re proceeding south! Prep a truck for recce and push it into the shade.
I've got this covered! Hold that perimeter!
Thought you were dead for sure. You all right?
You want out of here, right? No problem. We’ll bring a truck around, leave it for you here at the shelter. But there's a condition.
Situation in the north’s not good. They’re after us. Gotta figure out the next step.
We're done here! Mount up... Piet, you're riding with me... I'll explain on the way down...
The boat’s lined up. Everything’s set. I just need a man to ferry it through.
No. Not him. He talks too much. I need somebody with a lick of sense.
Welcome to Bowa-Seko. - Nice work, with Gakumba. The man deserved it.
Listen. I’m taking a bit of initiative here. The big boss, Major Tambossa, doesn’t know anything about it, and I’d like to keep it that way. - You follow?

Because here’s the thing. The situation being what it is these days, there’s a good chance the warlords in the South could join forces. If that happens, guaranteed, blokes like you and I are out of a job. Or worse - shot and dumped overboard like some rotten meat.

So. To keep that from happening, I’m going to stir the pot. - Turns out your friend the Jackal’s been hiding a massive weapons cache on his island. Lake Segolo. I’ve worked out a way to sail those weapons straight into the city - under a UFLL flag. Tambossa will assume the Front's to blame, and next thing you know, we’re back at it.
I’ve got a skipper. All the bribes have been arranged. All I need now is a man to ride along, keep an eye on the merchandise.
Good. Make your way to the island and rendezvous with the ferry. The skipper will handle the rest.
We’ll be back fighting this idiotic war in no time. And then I'll get you a meeting with the Major.

Look at this story on the television. These pictures of the children in our camps, dying of dysentery. It’s very sad. - You know, when people see these pictures, it will break their hearts. They will have to send money, to help.
It will. Eventually. But it has to come to US first. We know how to handle it.
None of it will ever get to those poor sods.
If you’re looking for a job, we’ve got one.
Good to meet you at last. I’ve heard a lot about you. We’d like to talk to you about a job.
The U-F-blah-blah is getting a lot of medicine from next door. - You know how?
By blackmail. - That’s how. They grabbed a shipment of - something important... Fuel or something. But the country next door is desperate. Will pay anything.
The neighbors purchased some natural gas. It’s sitting on a train now stuck at the depot. The plan is to blow up the tank cars and queer the deal.
Railyard’s about one and a half kilometers west of Pala, right on the edge of the desert.
So I have this idea. You blow up the train. OK?
Uh yes… the railyard is about one and a half kilometers west of Pala, right on the edge of the desert.
What we’d like you to do is go straight to the railyard and take out those natural gas cars.
Now here’s the thing. Tankers are durable. Small-arms fire isn't going to cut it. You’ve got to get right in there and use explosives.
You’re a professional, and you know damn well and good these cars are going to be fortified.
I DON'T suggest hitting them long-range. You'll want to get in close and plant explosives.
Then watch the big fire burn!
Once trains are gone, hey! - No more medicine.
It’s simple, really. Just go to the railyard and destroy those natural-gas cars.
No time for big guy to waste!
You know what the people are saying? They say that all of you are going to leave the country.
Just a bunch of lies. Don’t believe everything you hear. You paid us to do a job, eh? We’re going to do it.
The money brought Bastion to Africa. No more money, no more PMC.
Well then keep the ducats coming, and you won’t have a problem.
Yes, of course that is what matters. Not the work. Not the effort to build a stronger Africa.

Oh. Is that what you’re doing? Didn’t realize. When you send your boys off to do your dirty work, even scores, and then hire mercs when the soldier supply runs low. You reckon that’s making things better, do ya.
What Dr. Gakumba is trying to tell you is that we’ve got a job, and we’re looking for a freelancer to take it. Somebody like you, china.
Want a job, china? This one’s right up your alley. I’ve got a plan to hit the APR where they live.
The APR’s providing security for some European agribusiness. You know the type. Blokes in three-piece suits, eager to try some funny business with the local ecosystem, and no complaints.
So APR soldiers guard the farms, and in exchange, the company gives them all the rabbit food they can eat.
Bloody fighters over there are eating like kings these days. You know why?
They’re getting paid by this agribusiness outfit. Bit of quid pro quo.
APR guards the farms, and in exchange, the company gives them bushels of food.
WE would like YOU to put a stop to this treachery. The company farm is in the foothills east of town.
It’s immoral, what they’re doing there. contaminating the water, the land.
Sure, whatever. Point is that the APR’s got an advantage over us.
Now their soldiers are guarding the farm, east of town. In the middle is a set of greenhouses.
There’s a shed in there, between two greenhouses. It houses the irrigation pumps. You figure out a way to destroy them.
There’s a shed in there, between two greenhouses. It houses the irrigation pumps.
I’d like you to take it out. You’re clever. You’ll know exactly what to do.
Then the scientists will understand that the APR cannot offer protection - to anybody. If you can do the job, that is.
You get the gist, eh? Go to the greenhouse complex, find the shed with all the pipes, and take it out.
Payments in stones, same as always.
I guess we'll be working together again. Psych Ops today.
Good. A professional. Just what we need.

Michele, BMD: "It’s Michele Dachss. Your meeting is over? Meet me east of the railyard."

Michele, BMD: "It’s Michele. Meet me a half kilometer northeast of Mokuba..."

Michele, BMD: "I’m at the airfield now. Bring the tank to me here."
Michele, BMD: "He’s dead, isn’t he? - OK. Meet us at Lakeside."
Michele, BMD: "Perfect. Now all you have to do is attack the motorpool."
Michele, BMD: "Good. You have the ledger. You’ll find the gendarme at his frontier post."
Michele, BMD: "It's me. It worked. The paratroopers will be at the shantytown soon. I’ll see you there."
Michele, BMD: "Good work. The train is pulling out now. Full complement on board. In five minutes, I go. - Remember. Train is two miles up track from railyard. Cannot miss it."

Michele, BMD: "I went ahead to the oasis. It seemed like the only way we could be secure... But please hurry. The APR patrols won't stay away for much longer."
Michele, BMD: "OK. All the drivers have heard the news about your attack. They are coming back now. Come find me and you can see the explosion for yourself."

Michele, BMD: "OK. The soldiers are in range. I think they have found the contraband. - Merde. If the APR finds out I’ve wagered their goods, I’ll be in trouble. I’ll need your help if things go badly."
Michele, BMD: "I got him -- ! Where are you? I need you here!"
Michele, BMD: "I’ve been shot down! They’ve got me pinned! Where the fuck are you?!"
Michele, BMD: "You just decided to do things your own way? You know, there are other things at stake, than just... Anyway. I'm going."

Michele, BMD: "I’ve got them! - Meet me as quick as you can!"
Michele, BMD: "The APR men found out! - I’m surrounded! Where are you?!"
Michele, BMD: "Don't tell me you lost your nerve? All right. I'll find another way."
Michele, BMD: "That's it then? It's okay. There will be other times."
Michele, BMD: "You changed your mind -- or what? No matter. I better get myself out of here."

Nasreen: "This is Nasreen. Please meet me up the hill from the Lake Segolo levee."

Nasreen, BND: "The plane is on its way. I’ll have the package soon."

Nasreen, BND: "What are you doing -- ? Fine. Keep ignoring my advice."

<tsk> Guy could have made way more money if he wanted to.

<whistle> This guy’s not kidding around with the merchandise! Look at this gun. -  “The Jackal.” What kind of name is that. - Guy is crazy! He practically give these things away! Why did he sell them so cheap?
They were cheap for the UFLL, too.
You good with a gun? You think you can hit a guy in a fast car?
It’s a big target. It’ll be easy to hit…
Is Kouassi talking to you, Quiepo? - No. He is talking to new guy.
Boss called. Said, “kill constable.” Hey! “No problem,” I said. “I know a guy.” You. Cause you’re hard.
He would be good. People know him.
You want a job? We got one. It’s good!
This man. This constable. He says he is going to give his men to UFLL.
Why? Why do this? APR is the greatest! - So you shoot him. OK? Then everybody knows how great APR is!
Quiepo. Tell him where to find this man.
He’s riding in a motorcade. It’s a moving target. You’ll have to pick a spot on the road and wait for him to come to you.
That little peanut will be in a great - big - SUV.
Tambossa told us where you can find this guy.
He’s in a motorcade. Couple of escort cars, lots of weapons. Best bet is to pick a spot and ambush him when he comes by.
Very easy. Not too many motorcades in this country of mine!
Ambush the motorcade and kill the cop. - And make it messy. We need you to send a message.
If you want, you kill all the guards too. Hey. No problem. - But be sure you get the constable. And do it so people see. OK? Everybody needs to know what happened!
I’ve got a good feeling about this. How bout we pay you right now for the work. Hm?
Ambush the motorcade, kill the police chief, and the job is complete.
People say a lot of crazy things.
I heard he’s got cancer, and only three months to live.
I also heard that somebody was paid to come here and kill him.
Who. The Jackal? - Come on. Guy’s an arms dealer. Who would want to kill a guy like that.
Well don’t just stand there. Come on in.
Sure. Maybe. - You want to make some money, son?
I’ve heard things about you. Terrible, evil things.
What the hell have you been doing, boy? They’ve been talking about you in every bodega from here to Katmandu! We’ve got some business to discuss.

So here’s the situation. - The UFLL has got a motor pool, over by the landfill. They use the place to fix their vehicles. - It’s all duct tape and baling wire over there, but somehow they manage to make it work.
We’re planning an attack on the UFLL motor pool. There are a hell of a lot of their vehicles on the road.
You know where the landfill is, right? Just west of here.
The motor pool’s over by the landfill, west of town. You can’t miss it. You sure as hell can’t miss the smell.
We need you to raise some hell. Take out their gear, set some stuff on fire…you get the idea. Just be sure you take out their air compressors. You copy? That’s the mission.

We - meaning Prosper and I - want you to find that motor pool and take it out. - This is fielder’s choice, all right? You handle it any way you like. It’s none of my damn business. Just be sure you take out their air compressors.
Today, you are being paid to blow things up! Tell me you do not love your job.
Here’s your money. Now get on out to that landfill and destroy those compressors.
Hey wow somebody is too important for us!
Yeah ok. Chop chop. I get it.
I consider it a serious problem. It would be easy for people to assume that I ordered this attack.
Look at their gear. Look what they’ve got. Jesus. That is highest quality.

If the people think I brought in this Special Forces team, then they will say: Gakumba is rich, taking their money and hiding it in secret bank accounts! Gakumba is buying entire armies, as easy as food off a shelf!
I wish you were rich. Then we would have some whoo-boy great stuff.
Damn. Look at that gun. I wonder if the Jackal can get us that.
How you get across border. Nobody can come into country these days.
You’re still around. Good. We need freelancer.
I need a man who can take a job and keep his mouth shut about it.
Nah. This guy doesn’t talk. He’s a pro.
You are a big man. Important. People talk to you. What are they saying about me?
Nobody knows nothing. Let’s talk business.
There is a Special Forces outfit in area. Just gun-for-hire guys. But they are armed to the teeth. They are paid to parachute in and grab someone -
He doesn’t need to know who.
There is a Special Forces team. Mercenaries. Extremely well equipped, these men.
They are here for a bigshot from the APR. But if they take our enemy, we got nobody to fight!
The SF team has set up in good position. In the desert. Two kilometers to southeast.
This team is waiting in the desert. Perhaps two kilometers southeast of here.
Here’s the problem. They’re here to take somebody from APR. And if they do it, people will think Gakumba planned it.
Gakumba here doesn’t want anybody to think HE plan secret rendition. Would make him look bad.
Enough please. All you have to do is find these men and destroy their vehicles.
The GEAR in their vehicle. Radios, water canteens, ammo, all that gear they dropped in.
Then people will think I am working with outsiders. This is no good!
So you must find their hiding-place and destroy their supplies.
Tough guys not so tough if they don’t have any bullets or MREs or water.
This is OUR struggle. Africa is for Africans. We do not need outside involvement! - I expect you to stop these men. Job is yours.
Standby point is in southern desert. Find the team and destroy their gear. Then they are nice and screwed. Payment's here.
So we’ll get to the point.
How did you let this happen?
Thank you for thinking that I control everything in this country.
Marron! This is obscene! They going to take that gold and won’t be nothing left! - WE were the ones. That old king came to us.
He talked to everybody. APR and UFLL. He has always played both ends against the middle. That is why he has the gold and we have this war.
This is wrong. APR’s gonna take all the gold. Then where we gonna be? Damn.
You want a job? We need a no-name scumbag like you.
You got some good timing, man.
You’re that guy. I been hearing about you.
Hey! Where have you been? We need to get you in with us.
You know this FUBAR country used to have a king? - I’m serious, man.
The hombre got a boatload of money from Europe, back in the day. And then he took off. But he’s back and he brought his gold with him.
Carbonell is very enthusiastic because our former king has returned.
And he brought his money with him.
Yes. Kgosi wants to return to his throne. He thinks it can be bought.
That gold comes from our mines. It belongs to us.
The gold is sitting out in an oasis in the northeastern desert. Millions of dollars! Sitting under a tarp!
All of it protected" by those stupid APR boys."
Hell YES it can be bought! - I'll sell it to him.
The gold is out at the northeastern oasis. The APR is guarding it.
Kgosi has brought his treasure to broker a peace agreement. What he doesn’t realize is that this is not possible.
We need some noname cabron like you to go out there and find the gold. Send a text message with the location.
Don't touch the treasure. It’s not yours.
Too much for one guy to carry, anyway.
We are not hiring you to take the gold. Only to kill the men guarding it.
Of course, we cannot send our men on this job. It must be an outside party. Like yourself.
Just need you to find it and text us the location on your mobile phone. That’s it.
The king thinks he can restore his legacy before he dies. Pass his throne on to his son. It will never happen. Not in my lifetime.
Got it? Hit the oasis. Kill the guards. Use your mobile to send us the location. It’s gonna be good.
Do not let us hold you up, sir.
You just completed your last mission for the APR.
This conflict with the APR. It has been going on for a long time. - Both sides tolerate the conflict, because we understand it.

But things have changed. You have changed them. The UFLL is almost unstoppable here - Even the party leader doesn't realize. So. I’ve decided to eliminate Kouassi and assert our control in the north. I will be the voice of stability. And peace.
You are the only person for this job.
It will only take one bullet.
Together, you and I can steer the future of this country.
Oh ho! Look who is here. The guy who works with everybody. - Well that’s about to end.
This is a good day for us, my friend!
You know, this thing with the UFLL, it has been going on a long time. - Both sides are used to it! Everybody understands it!
But I am a man of vision. The big man - Major Tambossa - said so himself.
The APR is stronger now than ever before! - Thanks to YOU, my friend! - So how about we make a REAL change. Destroy the UFLL in the north, once and for all!
You are the perfect one for the job.
He’s at his cabin up on Thabamolaetsa. He thinks it is hidden. But I know the way. You just follow the river and take the trail up to Goka Falls.
You come back when you are done and we will have a drink to celebrate! Here.
And more to come. This is a very rich country. And soon it will be - our country!
Now question is, what do I do with you.
Things have taken a turn for the worse. Leboa-Seko’s a mess. We need to deal with it. And my men are no use in their condition.
You want out of here? No problem. We’ll bring a truck around, leave it for you here at the shelter. But I require something.
You seem all right. No stab wounds. Head still attached to your body.
Listen up! We’re proceeding south! Prep a truck for recce and push it into the shade.
I've got this covered! Hold that perimeter!
Thought you were dead for sure. You all right?
You want out of here, right? No problem. We’ll bring a truck around, leave it for you here at the shelter. But there's a condition.
Situation in the north’s not good. They’re after us. Gotta figure out the next step.
We're done here! Mount up... Piet, you're riding with me... I'll explain on the way down...
The boat’s lined up. Everything’s set. I just need a man to ferry it through.
No. Not him. He talks too much. I need somebody with a lick of sense.
Welcome to Bowa-Seko. - Nice work, with Gakumba. The man deserved it.
Listen. I’m taking a bit of initiative here. The big boss, Major Tambossa, doesn’t know anything about it, and I’d like to keep it that way. - You follow?

Because here’s the thing. The situation being what it is these days, there’s a good chance the warlords in the South could join forces. If that happens, guaranteed, blokes like you and I are out of a job. Or worse - shot and dumped overboard like some rotten meat.

So. To keep that from happening, I’m going to stir the pot. - Turns out your friend the Jackal’s been hiding a massive weapons cache on his island. Lake Segolo. I’ve worked out a way to sail those weapons straight into the city - under a UFLL flag. Tambossa will assume the Front's to blame, and next thing you know, we’re back at it.
I’ve got a skipper. All the bribes have been arranged. All I need now is a man to ride along, keep an eye on the merchandise.
Good. Make your way to the island and rendezvous with the ferry. The skipper will handle the rest.
We’ll be back fighting this idiotic war in no time. And then I'll get you a meeting with the Major.

Look at this story on the television. These pictures of the children in our camps, dying of dysentery. It’s very sad. - You know, when people see these pictures, it will break their hearts. They will have to send money, to help.
It will. Eventually. But it has to come to US first. We know how to handle it.
None of it will ever get to those poor sods.
If you’re looking for a job, we’ve got one.
Good to meet you at last. I’ve heard a lot about you. We’d like to talk to you about a job.
The U-F-blah-blah is getting a lot of medicine from next door. - You know how?
By blackmail. - That’s how. They grabbed a shipment of - something important... Fuel or something. But the country next door is desperate. Will pay anything.
The neighbors purchased some natural gas. It’s sitting on a train now stuck at the depot. The plan is to blow up the tank cars and queer the deal.
Railyard’s about one and a half kilometers west of Pala, right on the edge of the desert.
So I have this idea. You blow up the train. OK?
Uh yes… the railyard is about one and a half kilometers west of Pala, right on the edge of the desert.
What we’d like you to do is go straight to the railyard and take out those natural gas cars.
Now here’s the thing. Tankers are durable. Small-arms fire isn't going to cut it. You’ve got to get right in there and use explosives.
You’re a professional, and you know damn well and good these cars are going to be fortified.
I DON'T suggest hitting them long-range. You'll want to get in close and plant explosives.
Then watch the big fire burn!
Once trains are gone, hey! - No more medicine.
It’s simple, really. Just go to the railyard and destroy those natural-gas cars.
No time for big guy to waste!
You know what the people are saying? They say that all of you are going to leave the country.
Just a bunch of lies. Don’t believe everything you hear. You paid us to do a job, eh? We’re going to do it.
The money brought Bastion to Africa. No more money, no more PMC.
Well then keep the ducats coming, and you won’t have a problem.
Yes, of course that is what matters. Not the work. Not the effort to build a stronger Africa.

Oh. Is that what you’re doing? Didn’t realize. When you send your boys off to do your dirty work, even scores, and then hire mercs when the soldier supply runs low. You reckon that’s making things better, do ya.
What Dr. Gakumba is trying to tell you is that we’ve got a job, and we’re looking for a freelancer to take it. Somebody like you, china.
Want a job, china? This one’s right up your alley. I’ve got a plan to hit the APR where they live.
The APR’s providing security for some European agribusiness. You know the type. Blokes in three-piece suits, eager to try some funny business with the local ecosystem, and no complaints.
So APR soldiers guard the farms, and in exchange, the company gives them all the rabbit food they can eat.
Bloody fighters over there are eating like kings these days. You know why?
They’re getting paid by this agribusiness outfit. Bit of quid pro quo.
APR guards the farms, and in exchange, the company gives them bushels of food.
WE would like YOU to put a stop to this treachery. The company farm is in the foothills east of town.
It’s immoral, what they’re doing there. contaminating the water, the land.
Sure, whatever. Point is that the APR’s got an advantage over us.
Now their soldiers are guarding the farm, east of town. In the middle is a set of greenhouses.
There’s a shed in there, between two greenhouses. It houses the irrigation pumps. You figure out a way to destroy them.
There’s a shed in there, between two greenhouses. It houses the irrigation pumps.
I’d like you to take it out. You’re clever. You’ll know exactly what to do.
Then the scientists will understand that the APR cannot offer protection - to anybody. If you can do the job, that is.
You get the gist, eh? Go to the greenhouse complex, find the shed with all the pipes, and take it out.
Payments in stones, same as always.
I guess we'll be working together again. Psych Ops today.
Good. A professional. Just what we need.
The Major and I were just discussing what to do about the radio announcer.
The propaganda machine in this country is quite impressive, really.
Yes. Of course. - When it’s the UFLL broadcasting.
Let’s discuss a bit of business. - You’ve heard the radio. It’s outrageous, the lies.
I have a plan to shut down Liberation Radio. Once and for all.
We’re going to shut the station down. We’ve learned that they broadcast from a mobile vehicle. - That’s how they’ve managed to avoid our soldiers until now.
But at nine a.m. this morning, they parked their station over Weelegol village.
They are very crafty, these announcers. They do not use a building to broadcast.
They have a trailer. It is a radio station on the move! But today, we know where they are.
They are hiding in the rocks overlooking Weelegol Village. It is deserted. Nobody there to witness events.
I would like you to attack this radio trailer and silence their station.
You’re just one man. I understand it will be difficult. But at least you will have the element of surprise.
And it is a simple job. All you have to do is blow up one generator.
They have selected a good position. If I send an entire squad, they would see my men coming. They would have time to escape, defend themselves.
But you are just one man. You will have the element of surprise. And all you have to do is blow up one generator.
A man as strong and as fast as you will have no problem.
I hope you will consider our cause. The lies these men tell are helping no one.
Destroying the generator will cripple their transmitter. - Remember. You’re looking for Weelegol Village.
This is no way to treat a man in my position.
What is risky? It will not affect OUR people.
You’re in no shape to start a war with another country.
Who says there will be a war? Mr. Greaves, you are too literal. WE will not be responsible for this horrible travesty.
No! Our prayers will go out to the unfortunate victims of this tragedy.
This will UNITE us. One Africa. Now do you see? We need this right now. Too much unrest on the streets. This will FOCUS people on what is important.
Hard to believe you’ve managed to survive this long.
Ah. I remember you. Rather difficult to forget.
This is the perfect man for this job.
Knows how to keep his mouth shut.
We need someone to rupture a pipeline.
No. Addi Mbantuwe's people are pumping water over the border, in exchange for large cash payments.
I hear you know how to work with explosives. We need a man to shut down a large pipeline.
Mbantuwe is selling freshwater to our neighbors. The UFLL will not profit at the expense of our people.
The pipeline’s being serviced at the moment, so it’s quite vulnerable.
You’ll find your weak point at the construction site. About half a kilometer west of the pumping station on Lake Segolo.
The pipeline is going to suffer a total and complete system failure. And soon.
Of course we would never be involved in such a thing. It must be the work of a free agent.
This pipe is huge. Will require large explosives.
You’ll find suitable demolitions at the TaeMoCo mine.
But the mine is in enemy territory, my friend. West of here. You’ll have to be very careful.
The pipe is most vulnerable at the construction site. Maybe two-hundred meters inland from the lake.
But first, you will travel to the TaeMo diamond mine and... liberate some TNT.
The mine is in enemy territory. This will not be an easy mission.
Greaves worries. He thinks of the people who rely on that water.
But this is wartime. Suffering is unavoidable, eh? It is for the greater good. For a stronger Africa.
The money’s in here. You’ll find the explosives at the diamond mine demo shed and the pipeline target at the construction site.
Greaves. I thought you said this was a friend.
…That’s what I’m trying to tell you. He didn’t SELL the weapons this time. He GAVE them away.
That’s ridiculous. He’s an arms dealer. He has to sell the weapons to live.
And now he’s gone. He’s up to something. I’m telling you.
Enough. I want you to focus on the real problem at hand - the people! They are no longer listening to us. Defying our orders. THEY are the threat, Greaves. Not this Jackal person.
Right. Good. We’ve been looking for someone like you.
He’s a free agent. - no ties to us.
Good to see you again. You’re just what we need. Important job today.
You said you wanted a free agent for the job. That’s your man, right there. Best there is.
There’s a serious morphine shortage in this country. The stuff just can’t be found.
People get desperate when it’s time for surgery. They’ll use anything to dull the pain. Whisky. Aerosol fumes. Saw a man drink paint thinner, once.
We are going to severely limit the supply of anesthetic in this country. We are tired of surgeries and miraculous recoveries.
When we shoot our enemies, we want them to die in the street. Not recuperate in a hospital, with pretty nurses around.

This shortage helps us, frankly. Less surgeries, less soldiers surviving. The UFLL has a small quantity of nitrous oxide. We’d like you to destroy it. The gas tanks are at an old dental clinic, west of Port Selao.
There are several nitrous-oxide tanks stacked outside a former dental clinic, west of Mosate-Selao.
They’re sitting on a flatbed truck, right in the street.
You see? Sometimes, they make it too easy.
The tanks are stacked high as your chest on a flatbed truck. They’re right out there for everyone to see.
A stationary target, one that won’t fight back. Think you can handle that?
You can destroy these tanks any way you see fit. Use your imagination. Just make sure they are ALL destroyed.
We will see how smoothly their surgeries go when the patients are still awake. Eh?
Mr. Greaves here has learned to accept the nature of our work! You must always look for the advantage!
We’ll pay in stones, same as always. Just so we’re clear: Go to the dental clinic and take out those nitrous tanks.
Big man. Does what he wants.
I assure you, Greaves. I have thought this through. It’s for the best.
Easy for you to say. You’re sitting in the first seat. - Now I’m warning you: don’t even THINK about shutting me out. I’ve done too much for this outfit.
This is the worst idea I’ve heard in a long time.
Come in, my friend. I have excellent news.
I hear you have been working for the UFLL! - It’s all right, come in, we are all friends here.
I’ve been in contact with Mbantuwe. We have decided that it’s time to bring an end to this conflict. The people are troubled. Too much unrest. It has to end.
Here. I want you to take this to Mbantuwe. He is at the Seko Brewery. Tell him I accept his terms. - Go on. Take it.
In exchange, he will give you a diamond attaché case. Bring it here, and then we will know that we have a good-faith arrangement.
Best watch your back, mate". Times are changing."
The boat’s lined up. Everything’s set. I just need a man to ferry it through.
No. Not him. I need a man who can keep his bloody mouth shut.
Good! You made it. - And Kouassi’s dead. - So now the question is, what’s our next move.
Never mind. I think I just solved my problem.
- We’re on our own. Only way any of us are going to make it is if we plan ahead.
Did you hear? Bastion UK packed up and left the country. - That’s right. I spent ten years leading most of those boys in Angola, and look how they repay me.
I’ve been thinking about it. There’s a good chance the warlords in Bowa-Seko will decide to join forces. End the conflict for a while. If that happens, soldiers like you and I are fucked.
The men in charge always manage to get by.
It’s the foot-soldiers that get lined up against the wall and shot. Every time.
So! We’re going to keep that from happening. Turns out your friend the Jackal’s got a huge stockpile of weapons hidden on an island near Port Selao.
We’re going to bring them into the city. Give them to all the locals. And under an APR flag, too. I reckon that’ll force my boss to get his head back in the game.
Let’s get things started up again. Let’s face it: we need the business.
I’ve got a captain to handle the boat. Now I just need someone I can trust to escort the goods.
How about it. You interested? I can get you a meeting the big man. Addi Mbantuwe.
Could be the best thing, really. I mean the hell with Bastion.
Too bad to be left behind like that.
Nobody asked you. There are still plenty of men in-country. They’ll work with me for sure. They need the money.
They’ll work for ME, you mean.
As long as you pay, Addi. God knows you’ve got the work.
That’s right. These civilians are a problem. We’re going to get them under control. I don’t like the way things are going. It’s no longer safe.
You still sick? Not going to waste my time on a sick man.
He looks healthy enough. Reckon he’ll do.
Ho. - How's it? You ready for a job or what?
Malaria situation’s out of control. Turns out that the APR’s got a lock on some sort of remedy.
A plant that grows here. Artemisia. A very potent plant. Our medicine men know exactly how to use it.
The APR has got an advantage over us. They have found a way to use this herb, the Artemisia plant, to help their soldiers who are suffering from malaria. We would like to take away their advantage.
Everybody’s getting sick these days. It’s a bloody plague.
Ya. Anyway as I was saying, the APR’s got a system for drying out the plant, turning it into medicine.
They’ve got these kilns, see. Up in the Dogon cliff-village.
Yes. They’re using kilns to dry out the plant, turn it into medicine powder. These kilns are way up in the Dogon village.
You know it, I reckon. Maybe you already killed a few men there.
We’d like YOU to smash these kilns into bits.
We would like you to find a way up into the village and destroy the kilns. All of them.
This is Tambossa’s fault. He is to blame, with his selfishness and favoritism. If the APR want to know where their medicine has gone, they need only look at their leader!
Just so we're clear: Go to the Dogon cliff-dwellings and destroy the kilns.
Enough of that. I don’t want to hear that man’s name again.
They won’t. Look what they did to ME. Left me high and dry.
You should talk to Bastion. Tell them to come back.
The Jackal’s come over them, that’s what. I’m telling you. He’s up to something.

We are in a dangerous situation. You walk in the streets, you can feel that something could happen with the civilians at any moment. They dare to show me anger. Defy my orders. I do not know what’s come over them.
Come on. We’ve got work. - Going after an arms dealer today.
Bit of a specialty of yours, as I recall.
